messages.content: You improve the prompt templates of a small (1.5B-parameter) code model. The model and its sampling are frozen; only the template text may change. Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else.

ROUND 1.

Rules for every template you write:
- It must contain exactly these placeholders, each written as {name}: {task_prompt} {examples} {solution_format} {language}. No other braces.
- It must keep the line "Required solution format:" immediately followed by a newline and {solution_format}.
- It may be at most 400 characters longer than the frozen template it replaces. Shorter is allowed; a 1.5B model follows short instructions better.
- Text must be TASK-INDEPENDENT: no facts, hints or algorithms for any particular task, no example solutions.
- The answer must still end with ONE fenced code block in {language} (the extractor takes the last fenced block).

FROZEN TEMPLATES (current text):
{
 "qwen_sample_v2": "{task_prompt}\n\nPublic examples (input and expected output):\n{examples}\n\nRequired solution format:\n{solution_format}\n\nThink step by step, then give your final complete solution in {language} as ONE fenced code block. The code block must be the last thing in your answer.",
 "qwen_sample_v2b": "{task_prompt}\n\nPublic examples (input and expected output):\n{examples}\n\nRequired solution format:\n{solution_format}\n\nIn your reasoning, first list the edge cases (empty or minimal inputs, boundary values, duplicates, large inputs) and work out a simple brute-force way to check the public examples by hand. Then derive the efficient solution and check it against both. Then give your final complete solution in {language} as ONE fenced code block. The code block must be the last thing in your answer."
}

DEVELOPMENT TASKS the variants will be tried on (statements and public examples only):
[{"task_id": "P1-02", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": list of integers}. Return sum of elements divisible by 2, including negative even integers; empty list gives 0.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": []}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 2, 3, 4]}, "expected": 6}, {"input": {"nums": [-4, -3, 0, 5]}, "expected": -4}, {"input": {"nums": [7]}, "expected": 0}]}, {"task_id": "P1-04", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": list of integers, \"k\": nonnegative int}. Rotate right by k positions; preserve elements; empty list returns [].", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": [], "k": 100}, "expected": []}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 2, 3], "k": 0}, "expected": [1, 2, 3]}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 2, 3], "k": 4}, "expected": [3, 1, 2]}, {"input": {"nums": [9], "k": 99}, "expected": [9]}]}, {"task_id": "P1-06", "statement": "Input {\"a\": sorted integer list, \"b\": sorted integer list}. Return one nondecreasing merged list, retaining duplicates.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"a": [], "b": []}, "expected": []}, {"input": {"a": [1, 3], "b": [2, 4]}, "expected": [1, 2, 3, 4]}, {"input": {"a": [1, 1], "b": [1]}, "expected": [1, 1, 1]}, {"input": {"a": [-9, 0], "b": [-4, 5]}, "expected": [-9, -4, 0, 5]}]}, {"task_id": "P1-07", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": strictly increasing integer list}. Return maximal consecutive runs as [start,end] pairs, inclusive.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": []}, "expected": []}, {"input": {"nums": [1]}, "expected": [[1, 1]]}, {"input": {"nums": [-2, -1, 0, 4, 5]}, "expected": [[-2, 0], [4, 5]]}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 3, 5]}, "expected": [[1, 1], [3, 3], [5, 5]]}]}, {"task_id": "P1-09", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": list of integers}. Return the second-largest DISTINCT integer, or JSON null if fewer than two distinct values.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": []}, "expected": null}, {"input": {"nums": [3, 3]}, "expected": null}, {"input": {"nums": [5, 3, 5, 2]}, "expected": 3}, {"input": {"nums": [-1, -2, -3]}, "expected": -2}]}, {"task_id": "P1-12", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": NONEMPTY list of integers}. Return maximum sum of a contiguous nonempty subarray, including all-negative cases.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": [-3]}, "expected": -3}, {"input": {"nums": [-5, -2, -7]}, "expected": -2}, {"input": {"nums": [5, -10, 4, 7]}, "expected": 11}, {"input": {"nums": [0, 0, 0]}, "expected": 0}]}, {"task_id": "P1-29", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": nonempty int list, \"k\": int between 1 and len(nums)}. Return kth largest element counting duplicate occurrences.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": [1], "k": 1}, "expected": 1}, {"input": {"nums": [5, 5, 1], "k": 2}, "expected": 5}, {"input": {"nums": [-1, -4, 0], "k": 3}, "expected": -4}, {"input": {"nums": [8, 2, 9, 4], "k": 3}, "expected": 4}]}, {"task_id": "P1-30", "statement": "Input {\"temps\": integer list}. For each day return days until first STRICTLY warmer temperature to its right, or 0 if none.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"temps": []}, "expected": []}, {"input": {"temps": [4, 3, 2]}, "expected": [0, 0, 0]}, {"input": {"temps": [1, 2, 3]}, "expected": [1, 1, 0]}, {"input": {"temps": [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73]}, "expected": [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]}]}, {"task_id": "P1-35", "statement": "Input {\"heights\": list of nonnegative ints}. Return total water units trapped between histogram bars of unit width.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"heights": []}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"heights": [0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 1]}, "expected": 6}, {"input": {"heights": [4, 2, 0, 3, 2, 5]}, "expected": 9}, {"input": {"heights": [1, 2, 3]}, "expected": 0}]}, {"task_id": "P1-38", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": list of nonnegative integers}. Return whether nums can be split into two disjoint subsets with equal sums; empty list -> true.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": []}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 5, 11, 5]}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 2, 3, 5]}, "expected": false}, {"input": {"nums": [0, 0, 0]}, "expected": true}]}, {"task_id": "P1-39", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": NONEMPTY integer list}. Return maximum product of a contiguous, nonempty subarray, allowing negatives and zero.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": [-1]}, "expected": -1}, {"input": {"nums": [2, 3, -2, 4]}, "expected": 6}, {"input": {"nums": [-2, 0, -1]}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"nums": [-2, 3, -4]}, "expected": 24}]}, {"task_id": "P1-11", "statement": "Input {\"text\": string}. Check (), [], {} nesting and pairing; ignore all non-bracket characters. Return boolean.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"text": ""}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "([{}])"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "([)]"}, "expected": false}, {"input": {"text": "hello{(a+b)}!"}, "expected": true}]}, {"task_id": "P1-21", "statement": "Input {\"text\": string, \"pattern\": string}. Return whether entire text matches pattern, where ? matches exactly one character and * matches zero or more characters; all other chars literal. Characters such as [ ] . \\ ^ + ( ) are ordinary literals, not special.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"text": "", "pattern": "*"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "ab", "pattern": "a?"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "abcdef", "pattern": "a*f"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "abc", "pattern": "a*d"}, "expected": false}]}, {"task_id": "P1-23", "statement": "Input {\"text\": string} formatted as nested k[encoded_text] where k is nonnegative decimal, text atoms are lowercase letters, and bracket syntax is valid. Return fully expanded string; expanded length <= 2000. Nesting may be deeper than two levels, and k may have several digits or be 0.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"text": ""}, "expected": ""}, {"input": {"text": "3[a]"}, "expected": "aaa"}, {"input": {"text": "2[a2[b]]"}, "expected": "abbabb"}, {"input": {"text": "0[x]b3[c]"}, "expected": "bccc"}]}, {"task_id": "P1-26", "statement": "Input {\"tokens\": valid postfix expression list of decimal integer strings and +,-,*,/}. Return int result. Division truncates toward zero; divisor never zero; result fits signed 32-bit. Operands may be negative; division truncates toward zero also for negative operands.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"tokens": ["3", "4", "+"]}, "expected": 7}, {"input": {"tokens": ["7", "-3", "/"]}, "expected": -2}, {"input": {"tokens": ["4", "2", "5", "*", "+"]}, "expected": 14}, {"input": {"tokens": ["-3", "2", "*"]}, "expected": -6}]}, {"task_id": "P1-34", "statement": "Input {\"text\": string, \"pattern\": valid restricted regex}. Pattern supports . (any one char) and * (zero+ of preceding token). Match the ENTIRE text. Pattern never begins with * or contains consecutive *.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"text": "", "pattern": ""}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "aa", "pattern": "a*"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "ab", "pattern": ".*"}, "expected": true}, {"input": {"text": "mississippi", "pattern": "mis*is*p*."}, "expected": false}]}, {"task_id": "P1-16", "statement": "Input {\"grid\": rectangular list of strings containing characters 0 or 1}. Count connected components of 1 cells, using 4-neighbor adjacency. [] -> 0.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"grid": []}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"grid": ["0"]}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"grid": ["1"]}, "expected": 1}, {"input": {"grid": ["101", "010", "101"]}, "expected": 5}]}, {"task_id": "P1-28", "statement": "Input {\"grid\": rectangular matrix of integers 0=open or 1=blocked}. Return min 4-neighbor moves from top-left to bottom-right, or -1 if no path, blocked endpoint, or empty grid. An empty grid is [] or a grid whose rows are empty ([[]]).", "public_examples": [{"input": {"grid": []}, "expected": -1}, {"input": {"grid": [[0]]}, "expected": 0}, {"input": {"grid": [[1]]}, "expected": -1}, {"input": {"grid": [[0, 1], [0, 0]]}, "expected": 2}]}, {"task_id": "P1-37", "statement": "Input {\"grid\": rectangular matrix of nonnegative cell costs and -1 obstacles}. Move only right or down from top-left to bottom-right. Path cost includes endpoints. Return minimum cost, or null if no path/empty grid.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"grid": []}, "expected": null}, {"input": {"grid": [[2]]}, "expected": 2}, {"input": {"grid": [[0, 2], [1, 3]]}, "expected": 4}, {"input": {"grid": [[-1, 1], [1, 2]]}, "expected": null}]}, {"task_id": "P1-14", "statement": "Input {\"words\": list of lowercase words}. Group anagrams. Groups are ordered by first appearance; words within each group stay in original input order. The empty string may appear as a word; all empty strings form one group.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"words": []}, "expected": []}, {"input": {"words": ["eat", "tea", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat"]}, "expected": [["eat", "tea", "ate"], ["tan", "nat"], ["bat"]]}, {"input": {"words": ["a", "a"]}, "expected": [["a", "a"]]}, {"input": {"words": ["ab", "ba", "abc"]}, "expected": [["ab", "ba"], ["abc"]]}]}, {"task_id": "P1-20", "statement": "Input {\"capacity\": nonnegative int, \"ops\": list of [\"put\",key,value] or [\"get\",key] with integer keys/values}. Output the results of get commands; missing -> -1. Updating and successful get mark most recently used. Capacity zero stores nothing.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"capacity": 0, "ops": [["put", 1, 2], ["get", 1]]}, "expected": [-1]}, {"input": {"capacity": 1, "ops": [["put", 1, 4], ["put", 2, 5], ["get", 1], ["get", 2]]}, "expected": [-1, 5]}, {"input": {"capacity": 2, "ops": [["put", 1, 1], ["put", 2, 2], ["get", 1], ["put", 3, 3], ["get", 2]]}, "expected": [1, -1]}, {"input": {"capacity": 2, "ops": []}, "expected": []}]}, {"task_id": "P1-25", "statement": "Input {\"nums\": rotated strictly increasing integer list, \"target\": int}. Return target index or -1; empty list -> -1.", "public_examples": [{"input": {"nums": [], "target": 3}, "expected": -1}, {"input": {"nums": [4, 5, 1, 2, 3], "target": 2}, "expected": 3}, {"input": {"nums": [1, 2, 3], "target": 7}, "expected": -1}, {"input": {"nums": [1], "target": 1}, "expected": 0}]}]

OUTCOMES of earlier variants (runtime-visible only): none yet (first round).

Propose exactly TWO variants (Harness-style invariant / domain pair):
1. "general": a change to how the model approaches ANY task (planning, checking its own answer against the examples, staying concise).
2. "coding": a change specific to writing a Python solve(data) function (reading the input dictionary, edge cases, return types, avoiding printing).
Each variant gives full replacement texts for BOTH frozen templates.
JSON schema: {"variants": [{"name": "general", "qwen_sample_v2": "...", "qwen_sample_v2b": "...", "rationale": "one sentence"},
                           {"name": "coding",  "qwen_sample_v2": "...", "qwen_sample_v2b": "...", "rationale": "one sentence"}]}
